sections.title: NEW ENGLAND AND THE MID ATLANTIC STATES INTO THE TN VALLEY
sections.text: CONSIDERABLE AMPLIFICATION/INTENSIFICATION OF ERN CANADA/NERN U.S. TROUGH IS FORECAST THIS PERIOD WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT FEATURE OF NOTE BEING VIGOROUS SHORT WAVE TROUGH/MIDLEVEL JET STREAK WHICH WILL TRANSLATE THROUGH THE GREAT LAKES REGION TODAY AND ACROSS NEW ENGLAND TONIGHT. MESOSCALE MODEL GUIDANCE AND WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SUGGEST THE PRESENCE OF A WEAKER...PRECEDING IMPULSE WHICH WILL PROGRESS EWD FROM THE LOWER GREAT LAKES ACROSS NEW ENGLAND. AT THE SURFACE...SYNOPTIC COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO INTENSIFYING UPPER TROUGH WILL SHIFT EWD THROUGH NEW ENGLAND AND MORE SEWD THROUGH THE MID ATLANTIC STATES...OH/TN VALLEYS AND CNTRL APPALACHIANS. THIS BOUNDARY ALONG WITH PRE-FRONTAL/LEE TROUGH FROM ERN NEW ENGLAND INTO THE PIEDMONT REGION WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY FOCI FOR STRONG TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD. THE PRESENCE OF ONGOING STORMS FROM THE LOWER GREAT LAKES EWD INTO THE HUDSON VALLEY AND SRN NEW ENGLAND...AND FARTHER SW ALONG THE OH RIVER WILL RESULT IN RESIDUAL AREAS OF DENSER CLOUDINESS GOING INTO THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE. HOWEVER OUTSIDE OF THESE AREAS...THE COMBINATION OF BOUNDARY LAYER DEW POINTS IN THE 60S TO LOW/MID 70S AND DIABATIC HEATING WILL YIE

sections.title: SRN SD INTO THE CNTRL PLAINS
sections.text: DESPITE ANY MEANINGFUL HEIGHT FALLS/FORCING FORECAST ALOFT...MODEL GUIDANCE IS SUGGESTIVE THAT A SURFACE LOW WILL DEEPEN TODAY OVER THE NEB SAND HILLS..ALONG A WEAK W-E ORIENTED CONFLUENCE ZONE. ABUNDANT DAYTIME HEATING...COUPLED WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S TO LOW 60S AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT LATER THIS AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J/KG. GIVEN THE WEAK FORCING...EXPECT ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED STORM DEVELOPMENT INVOF SURFACE WAVE AND CONFLUENCE ZONE. OVERALL MAGNITUDE OF TROPOSPHERIC FLOW WILL REMAIN MARGINAL...THOUGH THE PRESENCE OF VERTICALLY-VEERING WIND PROFILES AND AROUND 30 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR MAY SUPPORT UPDRAFT ROTATION WITH A RISK FOR HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS IN THE STRONGER STORMS.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY INTO THE RED RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: DAYTIME HEATING COUPLED WITH MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER /I.E. DEW POINTS IN THE 70S/ WILL YIELD MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 1500-3000+ J/KG LATER TODAY. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN WEAK...THOUGH THE PRESENCE OF THE BOUNDARY AND MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY MAY SUPPORT A FEW INTENSE STORM CLUSTERS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 08/05/2010

sections.title: OH/TN VALLEYS EWD TO THE MID ATLANTIC THROUGH THIS EVENING
sections.text: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE ALREADY ONGOING NEAR A SEWD-MOVING COLD FRONT ACROSS KY...AND ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS LIKELY THIS AFTERNOON AS THE LOW LEVELS DESTABILIZE IN ADVANCE OF THE FRONT WITH STRONG SURFACE HEATING FROM TN/KY EWD INTO VA. THIS CORRIDOR WILL LIE ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF THE STRONGER WLY MIDLEVEL FLOW /30-35 KT/ WHICH WILL SUPPORT MULTICELL CLUSTERS AND LINE SEGMENTS. THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES WITH MLCAPE OF 2500-4000 J/KG...STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES BY AFTERNOON...AND SOME DRY AIR ALOFT WILL FAVOR STRONG DOWNDRAFTS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT THROUGH THIS EVENING...THOUGH ISOLATED/MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL CANNOT BE RULED OUT GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY.

sections.title: NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A DEEPENING MIDLEVEL LOW NEAR JAMES BAY WILL DRIVE A PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH EWD ACROSS NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON...FOLLOWED BY A COLD FRONT TONIGHT. RELATIVELY WIDESPREAD CLOUDS AND MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AOB 6 C/KM WILL TEND TO LIMIT THE MAGNITUDE OF INSTABILITY TODAY ACROSS NEW ENGLAND INVOF THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH. SOMEWHAT LARGER CLOUD BREAKS ARE APPARENT ACROSS SRN NEW ENGLAND AND ERN MAINE...WHERE SURFACE HEATING WILL BE STRONGEST AND AFTERNOON MLCAPE COULD REACH 1000-1500 J/KG WITH MINIMAL CONVECTIVE INHIBITION. THUS...EXPECT THE BAND OF PRE-FRONTAL CONVECTION NOW IN CENTRAL NY TO INTENSIFY SOME AS IT REACHES THE HUDSON VALLEY AROUND MIDDAY-EARLY AFTERNOON...WITH ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE FARTHER NE INTO MAINE. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT AND THE WEAK-MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL SUPPORT A THREAT OF ISOLATED DAMAGING GUSTS WITH PRIMARILY MULTICELL CLUSTERS THIS AFTERNOON.

sections.title: CENTRAL/WRN NEB THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A WEAK SURFACE TROUGH AND SURFACE HEATING WILL HELP FOCUS INSTABILITY AND WEAK LOW-LEVEL ASCENT THIS AFTERNOON IN THE AREAS NEAR AND N OF LBF. MLCAPE COULD REACH 1500-2000 J/KG WITH AFTERNOON TEMPERATURES IN THE LOW-MID 80S AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S. THOUGH LOW-LEVEL FLOW WILL REMAIN WEAK...DEEP-LAYER SHEAR IS AT LEAST MARGINALLY FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. A COUPLE OF STORMS MAY PRODUCE ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND STRONG GUSTS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING BEFORE INSTABILITY DIMINISHES.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A COUPLE OF THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS ARE ONGOING AS OF LATE MORNING IN SE LA AND SE AR. STRONG SURFACE HEATING OF A VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WILL AGAIN SUPPORT STRONG AFTERNOON INSTABILITY ON THE PERIPHERY OF THESE MORNING STORMS...IN A WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR ENVIRONMENT. ISOLATED WET MICROBURSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER STORMS THIS AFTERNOON...WITH CONVECTION POTENTIALLY FOCUSED IN LA/MS ALONG OUTFLOWS FROM THE MORNING STORMS. ..THOMPSON/GRAMS.. 08/05/2010

sections.title: 20Z UPDATE
sections.text: THE ONLY CHANGES TO THE PRIOR OUTLOOK CONCERN ADJUSTMENTS TO SEVERE PROBABILITIES ACROSS THE MID SOUTH AND NORTHEAST... ATTEMPTING TO BETTER REFLECT ONGOING CONVECTIVE TRENDS...AND INCREASING UNCERTAINTY CONCERNING SEVERE POTENTIAL ACROSS AREAS EAST OF THE LOWER GREAT LAKES INTO NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND.

sections.title: SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: A LOW AMPLITUDE MID-LEVEL IMPULSE EMBEDDED WITHIN THE WEAKER SOUTHERN BRANCH OF THE WESTERLIES IS IN THE PROCESS OF SHIFTING OFF THE NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC AND NEW ENGLAND COASTS. HOWEVER... AS A MUCH STRONGER NORTHERN BRANCH SHORT WAVE TROUGH DIGS THROUGH ONTARIO...A REMNANT AREA OF MID/UPPER FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION CONTINUES TO SUPPORT AN EVOLVING STORM CLUSTER OVER SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND. IN THE PRESENCE OF AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED MODERATE CAPE /1000-2000 J PER KG MIXED LAYER/ AND MODEST VERTICAL SHEAR BENEATH 30+ KT WESTERLY 500 MB FLOW... POTENTIAL FOR FURTHER CONSOLIDATION AND INTENSIFICATION OF CONVECTION EXISTS PRIOR TO ACTIVITY SPREADING OFFSHORE BY 21-22Z. THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT APPEARS TO BE THE RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS WITH AN ACCOMPANYING DEVELOPING SURFACE COLD POOL.

sections.title: LOWER GREAT LAKES THROUGH NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: THE RISK FOR SEVERE STORMS IS NOT COMPLETELY NEGLIGIBLE...AS DEEP LAYER WESTERLY MEAN FLOW STRENGTHENS TO 40-50 KT LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. BUT...NORTH OF A WEAK LEADING SURFACE FRONTAL ZONE EXTENDING FROM SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND WESTWARD INTO THE OZARK PLATEAU/SOUTHERN PLAINS...THE AIR MASS IS COOLER AND SLIGHTLY DRIER. COUPLED WITH WEAK LOW-LEVEL FOCUS/FORCING FOR CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT...AND STRONGER MID/UPPER FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THE ONTARIO SHORT WAVE NOT ARRIVING UNTIL LATE THIS EVENING...STORM COVERAGE IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN WIDELY SCATTERED AT BEST...AND PROBABLY ASSOCIATED WITH ACTIVITY GRADUALLY SPREADING EASTWARD FROM SOUTHERN ONTARIO AND QUEBEC.

sections.title: TENNESSEE VALLEY/CUMBERLAND PLATEAU INTO MID ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT WILL BECOME FOCUSED EAST OF THE BLUE RIDGE FOR THE LATE AFTERNOON HOURS. A VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER CHARACTERIZED BY MID/UPPER 70S DEW POINTS HAS BECOME STRONGLY HEATED WITH TEMPERATURES IN THE 90S TO AROUND 100F ACROSS MUCH OF VIRGINIA. IN THE PRESENCE OF LARGE CAPE /MIXED LAYER OF 3000-4000 J PER KG/ AND STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES... THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES APPEAR FAVORABLE FOR DOWNBURSTS AND STRONG SURFACE COLD POOLS WITH ONGOING CONVECTION NOW OCCURRING WITHIN THE LEE SURFACE TROUGH. CONSOLIDATION AND UPSCALE GROWTH APPEARS LIKELY DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...WITH EASTWARD MOTION ENHANCED BY A BELT OF 40 KT WESTERLY DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW NOW NOSING ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL APPALACHIANS AND NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC COAST REGION. ..KERR.. 08/05/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1128 AM CDT THU AUG 05 2010/
